thread:
ella: Quick Q — customer reports a failure and gave me request_id=ryz-831b. What's the fastest way to pull the raw request logs + the trace? need both for debugging.

sam: Two quick paths: console (UI) or CLI. Start with the console to see the trace link, then use stern/grep for raw lines.

sam: Console steps: Traces -> search for the request_id OR trace id. If you open a span, check attributes for k8s.pod_name / host / service. From there you can jump to Logs and set query: "request_id:\"ryz-831b\"" and narrow the time window.

ron: If you prefer CLI, common patterns: use stern to tail pods for the service then filter for the request id. Example:
```
stern -n prod "service-name" --timestamps | rg "ryz-831b"
```
If you don't know the service name yet, find it from the trace (service name on the span) or list pods by label:
```
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=service-name -o wide
```

sam: Also remember header names vary by client — we often emit X-Redwood-Request-Id or X-Request-Id. Try both in the logs search. Traces sometimes sample out, so you might find logs but no trace for older/sampled requests.

infra-bot: Tip: logs older than 30d may be archived to cold storage; if the request is >30d open an infra ticket.

mike: If you only have a trace_id, use Jaeger/Zipkin UI to open the trace -> click a representative span -> look for tags: k8s.pod_name, container_id, host. Once you have service/pod you can run a Loki query or grep the pod logs. Example Loki quick query: 
```
{app="service-name"} |= "ryz-831b"
```
Or a direct ES query (if you're using ES):
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LOG_API_TOKEN" -XPOST https://logs.redwood.internal/_search -d '{"query":{"match":{"request_id":"ryz-831b"}}}'
```

ron: Small debugging checklist:
- confirm client header (X-Request-Id vs X-Redwood-Request-Id)
- check time window +/- 2m from trace timestamp
- check service-level logs if edge/proxy already forwarded the id
- if nothing shows up, the request might be hitting the edge and getting rewritten — check edge logs (gateway namespace)

ella: super helpful. One more: is there a saved Console query/dashboard for this?

sam: Yup — we have a saved Logs query called "reqid-quick-hunt" in Observability -> Saved Queries. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/observability/saved-queries/reqid-quick-hunt (requires SSO). It sets the right filters + 5m window.

ron: If you get noisy results, try adding service:"service-name" and level:INFO to narrow it. Also if you see many matches, grep for the full UUID not the truncated id.

ella: OK grabbing the trace now and will run stern. Thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: FYI — if you need us to pull archived logs, ping infra with the team tag and request id.

ella: will do if needed, thanks!
